name: cc-stretch
description: Stretchtext replies for Claude Code: short by default, each phrase grows in place when you click it

startOn.title: Stretchtext on at start
startOn.description: Whether each session starts with stretchtext on: Claude gets the stretchtext guide in the system prompt, and stretches are drawn closed for you to open. Off, Claude gets no guide and every stretch is drawn open. /cc-stretch:stretch switches it for the session.

motion.title: Stretch motion
motion.description: How a stretch opens and closes: grow, its words arriving around the short form over 0.45 to 1.4 seconds; fast, the same in 0.2 seconds; instant, drawn open or closed at once; auto (the default), instant under a cc-stretch output style and grow under any other.

marks.title: Closed stretch marks
marks.description: Marks on a phrase you can open, as a list of bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, dim. Empty keeps the underline; none takes every mark away. Under a highlight, dim moves the text toward the highlight.

highlight.title: Closed stretch highlight
highlight.description: Background of a phrase you can open: a hex colour such as #264f78, in any case, or the word tinted, which highlights each closed stretch in the colour its words take once open, blended 75% into the background. Its text turns near black or near white, whichever reads better. Empty, or anything else, for none.

systemPromptGuide.title: Phrase guide in the system prompt
systemPromptGuide.description: Whether Claude gets the stretchtext phrase guide in the system prompt while stretchtext is on and no cc-stretch output style is active. Off, Claude gets no guide, and a setup with managed settings has no skipped hook to report for it. A cc-stretch output style holds its own rules either way.

filterWhileStreaming.title: Short forms while streaming
filterWhileStreaming.description: Whether a reply shows each stretch as its short form while it streams. Off, a stretch shows its markup until it closes, and a setup with managed settings has no skipped hook to report for it. The finished reply is drawn the same either way.
